Starter
decide how to begin
In h, begin by combining the two fractions inside the modulus into one fraction (use 10 as the common bottom).
Roots
ask why it works
In i, the right side is x. A modulus is never negative, so ask why x must be ≥ 0. Check both answers against that.
YOUR TURN
Solve g, h and i. Keep only the answers that pass your check.

Dyna Thinking Coach
Translator
turn words into numbers, pictures or steps
Write the two cases, for example 2x − 5x + 3 = 8 and = −8. Multiply both sides by the bottom.
Vault
pick what you already know
Remember: x can never be the value that makes a bottom 0. In c, first write 1 + x + 12x + 4 as one fraction.
YOUR TURN
Solve both cases in each part and write the answers.

Dyna Thinking Coach
Slicer
break it into small parts
In e and f, first get the modulus on its own, for example x − 5 = 8 − x. Then split into two cases.
Roots
ask why it works
Ask why some answers fail: a modulus cannot equal a negative number. So the other side must be ≥ 0 for each answer.
YOUR TURN
Solve, then cross out any answer that makes the other side negative.
